## Problem 1

```{r}
subway_df = 
  read_csv(
    "data/NYC_Transit_Subway_Entrance_And_Exit_Data.csv",
    col_types = cols(Route8 = "c", Route9 = "c", Route10 = "c", Route11 = "c")
  ) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  select(
    line, station_name, station_latitude, station_longitude, 
    starts_with("route"), entry, vending, entrance_type, ada
  ) |> 
  mutate(entry = entry == "YES")

dim(subway_df)

subway_df |> distinct(line, station_name) |> nrow()

subway_df |> filter(ada) |> distinct(line, station_name) |> nrow()

subway_df |> filter(vending == "NO") |> pull(entry) |> mean()

subway_long_df = 
  subway_df |> 
  pivot_longer(
    route1:route11,
    names_to = "route_number",
    names_prefix = "route",
    values_to = "route_name"
  ) |> 
  drop_na(route_name)

subway_long_df |> filter(route_name == "A") |> distinct(line, station_name) |> nrow()

subway_long_df |> filter(route_name == "A", ada) |> distinct(line, station_name) |> nrow()
```
The subway data contain one row for each station entrance/exit. I kept the necessary variables (line, station name, station latitude/longitude, route columns, entry, vending, entrance type, ADA compliance). I changed 'entry' from yes/no to true/false. The dataset has 1868 rows and 19 columns. The data are not tidy because the route served is in eleven columns instead of one variable. There are 465 stations (line and station name). Of them, 84 are ADA compliant. 37.7 percent of entrances and exits without vending allow entry. When I changed route columns into a route number and a route name, I determined 60 distinct stations serve the A train and 17 of them are ADA compliant.

## Problem 2
```{r}
trash_file = "data/202509 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx"

mr_df = 
  read_excel(trash_file, sheet = "Mr. Trash Wheel", range = cell_cols("A:N")) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  drop_na(dumpster) |> 
  mutate(
    sports_balls = as.integer(round(sports_balls)),
    year = as.numeric(year),
    trash_wheel = "Mr. Trash Wheel"
  )

prof_df = 
  read_excel(trash_file, sheet = "Professor Trash Wheel", range = cell_cols("A:M")) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  drop_na(dumpster) |> 
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year), trash_wheel = "Professor Trash Wheel")

gwynnda_df = 
  read_excel(trash_file, sheet = "Gwynns Falls Trash Wheel", range = cell_cols("A:L")) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  drop_na(dumpster) |> 
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year), trash_wheel = "Gwynnda")

trash_df = 
  bind_rows(mr_df, prof_df, gwynnda_df) |> 
  relocate(trash_wheel)

dim(trash_df)

trash_df |> 
  filter(trash_wheel == "Professor Trash Wheel") |> 
  pull(weight_tons) |> 
  sum()

trash_df |> 
  filter(trash_wheel == "Gwynnda", month == "June", year == 2022) |> 
  pull(cigarette_butts) |> 
  sum()
```
The combined dataset has 1188 observations and 15 variables. Key variables include the weight and volume of each dumpster and counts of items like cigarette butts. The total weight of trash collected by Professor Trash Wheel was 282.26 tons. Gwynnda collected 18,120 cigarette butts in June 2022.

## Problem 3
```{r}
baseline_raw_df = 
  read_csv("data/MCI_baseline.csv", skip = 1, na = c(".", "NA", "")) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  rename(
    baseline_age = current_age,
    education_years = education,
    onset_age = age_at_onset
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    sex = case_match(sex, 1 ~ "male", 0 ~ "female"),
    apoe4 = case_match(apoe4, 1 ~ "carrier", 0 ~ "non-carrier")
  )

baseline_df = 
  baseline_raw_df |> 
  filter(is.na(onset_age) | onset_age > baseline_age)

nrow(baseline_raw_df)

nrow(baseline_df)

sum(!is.na(baseline_df$onset_age))

mean(baseline_df$baseline_age)

baseline_df |> 
  filter(sex == "female") |> 
  summarize(prop = mean(apoe4 == "carrier"))

amyloid_df = 
  read_csv("data/mci_amyloid.csv", skip = 1, na = c("NA", "")) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  rename(id = study_id, time_0 = baseline) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    time_0:time_8,
    names_to = "years_since_baseline",
    names_prefix = "time_",
    values_to = "amyloid_ratio"
  ) |> 
  mutate(years_since_baseline = as.numeric(years_since_baseline))

dim(amyloid_df)

anti_join(baseline_df, amyloid_df, by = "id") |> nrow()

anti_join(amyloid_df, baseline_df, by = "id") |> distinct(id) |> nrow()

mci_df = inner_join(baseline_df, amyloid_df, by = "id")

dim(mci_df)

write_csv(mci_df, "data/mci_combined.csv")
```

Starting with the baseline data, I skipped the first descriptive row on import, treated `.` as missing, and recoded sex and APOE4 carrier status as text rather than numeric values. I removed 4 participants who already had MCI at baseline. 483 participants were recruited, and 479 met the inclusion criteria. Of them, 93 developed MCI. The average baseline age is 65.03 years. 30% of women are APOE4 carriers. I also skipped the descriptive first row for the longitudinal biomarker data and changed the visit columns into one long time variable. This resulted in 2435 rows and 3 columns (`id`, `years_since_baseline`, `amyloid_ratio`). Eight participants appear only in the baseline data; 16 appear only in the biomarker data. Combining the two datasets and keeping only participants in both gives 2355 rows and 8 columns. I saved this as `data/mci_combined.csv`.
